accepted.s: With reference to the distribution of black soils in the Deccan Plateau, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Very deep black soils are concentrated in the eastern Deccan Plateau and become deeper towards the south.
Black soils occur only along the coastal plains of the Deccan Plateau.
Very deep black soils occur in the north-western Deccan Plateau and become thinner towards the east and south.
Black soils are uniformly deep throughout the Deccan Plateau.
accepted.x: Very deep black soils are found in the north-western Deccan Plateau. They become medium, thin and shallow towards the east and south.
accepted.tq: Use the location and directional trend to distinguish the correct geographical statement.
accepted.sec: Black soil depth variation across the Deccan and suited crops

accepted.s: Which one of the following groups consists entirely of crops associated with black soil cultivation?
o: Tea, coffee, rubber, coconut and arecanut
Rice, sugarcane, jute, tea and coconut
Cotton, jowar, chillies, tobacco and oilseeds
Barley, apple, saffron, tea and rubber
accepted.x: Black soils, also called black cotton soils, are suited to cotton, jowar, chillies, tobacco, oilseeds and wheat. They are also suitable for dry farming.
accepted.tq: Select the option containing only crops linked with the soil under consideration.
accepted.sec: Black soil depth variation across the Deccan and suited crops

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding black soils in Andhra Pradesh:
1. They occupy about one-fourth of the land area of the State.
2. Deep black soils occur at Adoni and Alur.
3. The Kunderu basin and parts of Guntur, Palnadu, Prakasam and Kurnool contain black soils.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Black soils cover about 25% of Andhra Pradesh, with deep black soils at Adoni and Alur and important areas in the Kunderu basin, Guntur, Palnadu, Prakasam and Kurnool.
accepted.tq: Combine the area, location and distribution statements before selecting the coded option.
accepted.sec: Black soil depth variation across the Deccan and suited crops

accepted.s:
Which of the following crops are specifically mentioned in relation to black soils of Andhra Pradesh?
1. Cotton
2. Maize
3. Chillies
4. Turmeric
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Cotton, maize, chillies and turmeric are all grown in the black-soil regions of Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Check the complete crop list rather than selecting only the best-known black-soil crop.
accepted.sec: Black soil depth variation across the Deccan and suited crops

accepted.s: Peaty and marshy soils are generally formed under which of the following conditions?
o: Moderate rainfall, steep slopes and rapid erosion
Heavy rainfall, high humidity, waterlogging and accumulation of organic matter
Arid climate, wind deposition and alkaline irrigation
Low rainfall, intense evaporation and deficient drainage
accepted.x: Peaty and marshy soils form in areas of heavy rainfall and high humidity where waterlogging permits organic matter to accumulate.
accepted.tq: Match the soil type with its characteristic climatic and drainage conditions.
accepted.sec: Peaty/marshy soils - climatic conditions and areas

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT an area associated with peaty or marshy soils?
accepted.x: Peaty and marshy soils occur in Kerala, the Sundarbans, coastal Odisha and Tamil Nadu, north Bihar and Almora. Western Rajasthan is not listed among these areas.
accepted.tq: Find the geographically incongruous area among the listed soil regions.
accepted.sec: Peaty/marshy soils - climatic conditions and areas

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes peaty soils from saline soils?
o: Peaty soils form mainly due to excessive evaporation in deserts.
Peaty soils are associated with waterlogging and organic accumulation, whereas semi-arid conditions with salinity describe saline soils.
Peaty soils are formed only in semi-arid regions with salinity.
Peaty soils are always alkaline and contain no organic matter.
accepted.x: Peaty soils are black, heavy and highly acidic, forming under waterlogged, humid conditions. Semi-arid climate with salinity is characteristic of saline soils, not peaty soils.
accepted.tq: Separate the similar-looking climatic descriptions by linking each to its correct soil type.
accepted.sec: Peaty/marshy soils - climatic conditions and areas

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Alkaline soil — lime as the principal amendment
Acidic soil — salt-tolerant crops as the sole reclamation measure
accepted.x: Gypsum is used to reclaim alkaline or sodic soils, while lime is used for acidic soils. Drainage, leaching and salt-tolerant crops can also assist reclamation.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure amendment-soil pair and eliminate the reversed combinations.
accepted.sec: Problem soils - saline and alkaline soil reclamation (gypsum, lime), Karewa soils and their crop

accepted.s: Karewa soils are best described as:
o: Wind-deposited sandy soils of western Rajasthan
Lacustrine deposits forming plateaus above the Jhelum plains in the Kashmir Valley
Black cotton soils formed over basalt in the Deccan
Recent alluvial deposits of the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta
accepted.x: Karewas are old lake-bed deposits of unconsolidated gravel and mud. They form plateau-like surfaces above the Jhelum plains in the Kashmir Valley and are also found in the Bhadarwah valley.
accepted.tq: Use the origin and landform description to identify the correct soil type.
accepted.sec: Problem soils - saline and alkaline soil reclamation (gypsum, lime), Karewa soils and their crop

accepted.s: Karewa soils are particularly famous for the cultivation of:
accepted.x: Karewas are famous for saffron cultivation around Pampore. Almonds and walnuts are also associated with them, and high-density apple planting is expanding on these deposits.
accepted.tq: Identify the signature crop associated with a distinctive regional soil.
accepted.sec: Problem soils - saline and alkaline soil reclamation (gypsum, lime), Karewa soils and their crop

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements regarding land degradation is/are correct?
1. Salinity can hinder water and nutrient uptake by plants.
2. Salinity can break up soil structure and pollute water bodies.
3. Alkalinity may result from limestone or basalt parent material and alkaline irrigation water.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Salinity affects plant water and nutrient uptake, damages soil structure and may pollute water bodies. Alkalinity can be associated with limestone or basalt parent material and alkaline irrigation water.
accepted.tq: Test the effects and causes separately before choosing the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Land degradation - salinity, alkalinity, waterlogging - causes, affected states, reclaiming agents

accepted.s: The major cause of salinity, alkalinity and waterlogging in irrigated areas is:
o: Scientific irrigation combined with adequate drainage
Excessive crop rotation and contour farming
accepted.x: Unscientific irrigation practices combined with inadequate drainage promote salinity, alkalinity and waterlogging.
accepted.tq: Identify the cause-effect relationship rather than a reclamation measure.
accepted.sec: Land degradation - salinity, alkalinity, waterlogging - causes, affected states, reclaiming agents

accepted.s: Without adequate preservation measures, what proportion of the world's arable land could be affected by 2050 according to the stated projection?
accepted.x: The stated projection is that 50% of the world's arable land could be affected by 2050 if soil resources are not preserved.
accepted.tq: Read the projected percentage carefully and distinguish it from nearby plausible figures.
accepted.sec: Land degradation - salinity, alkalinity, waterlogging - causes, affected states, reclaiming agents

accepted.s: Which one of the following groups contains the states identified as affected by salinity and alkalinity problems?
o: Gujarat, Maharashtra, Odisha, Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand
Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Goa, Assam and Sikkim
Rajasthan, Haryana, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar
Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Meghalaya, Nagaland and Manipur
accepted.x: The affected states listed are Rajasthan, Haryana, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar. Canal-irrigated Punjab experienced salinity and alkalinity after the Green Revolution.
accepted.tq: Use the complete regional grouping to avoid substituting neighbouring states.
accepted.sec: Land degradation - salinity, alkalinity, waterlogging - causes, affected states, reclaiming agents

accepted.s: Which of the following is the most appropriate combination for reclaiming alkaline soil and curing waterlogging, respectively?
o: Organic litter alone and increased irrigation
Salt addition and land raising without drains
accepted.x: Gypsum is used with water management to reclaim alkaline soil. Waterlogging is addressed through drains, land levelling and tolerant crop varieties.
accepted.tq: Match each problem with its specific reclamation measure instead of reversing the remedies.
accepted.sec: Land degradation - salinity, alkalinity, waterlogging - causes, affected states, reclaiming agents

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the five classical factors of soil formation?
accepted.x: The five classical factors are parent material, climate, relief or topography, organisms and time. Latitude is not included in this five-factor list.
accepted.tq: Recall the standard five-factor framework and identify the extra term.
accepted.sec: Soil formation factors - parent rock, climate, relief, organisms, time

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about soil formation in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Climate, altitude and bedrock influence soil formation.
2. Andhra Pradesh soils are mainly a mixture of sand, silt and clay.
3. Silt deposited by the Godavari, Krishna and Pennar contributes to soil formation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Andhra Pradesh soil formation reflects climate, altitude, bedrock and river deposits, while its soils mainly comprise sand, silt and clay.
accepted.tq: Combine general soil-forming factors with the State-specific examples.
accepted.sec: Soil formation factors - parent rock, climate, relief, organisms, time

accepted.s: Which one of the following represents the approximate volume composition of a good soil?
o: Mineral matter 45%, organic matter 5%, water 25%, air 25%
Mineral matter 50%, organic matter 25%, water 15%, air 10%
Mineral matter 25%, organic matter 45%, water 25%, air 5%
Mineral matter 5%, organic matter 45%, water 25%, air 25%
accepted.x: A good soil is approximately composed of 45% mineral matter, 5% organic matter, 25% water and 25% air by volume.
accepted.tq: Check that all four components and their percentages are correctly paired.
accepted.sec: Soil composition - components for plant growth, organic matter and water holding

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about soil organic carbon is correct?
o: It binds soil particles into aggregates, raises infiltration and feeds microbes.
It reduces the water-holding capacity of clay soils in all conditions.
It disperses soil particles and reduces microbial activity.
It occurs mainly in sandy subsoil and is absent from topsoil.
accepted.x: Soil organic carbon binds particles into aggregates, improves infiltration and supports microbial activity. Clay soils hold more organic carbon than sandy soils, and topsoil holds the most.
accepted.tq: Choose the option describing the functions of the soil component rather than an opposite effect.
accepted.sec: Soil composition - components for plant growth, organic matter and water holding

accepted.s: India's average soil organic carbon reportedly declined over a period of 70 years from:
accepted.x: The reported decline in India's average soil organic carbon was from 1% to 0.3% over 70 years.
accepted.tq: Watch for reversal of the initial and final values in the percentage pair.
accepted.sec: Soil composition - components for plant growth, organic matter and water holding

accepted.s: Which one of the following soil orders occupies the largest share of India's area in the ICAR/USDA classification?
accepted.x: Inceptisols are the largest soil order in the stated classification, covering approximately 39.7% of India's area.
accepted.tq: Identify the largest category from the comparative area distribution.
accepted.sec: ICAR/USDA classification - soil orders by area, soil profile horizons

accepted.s:
Arrange the following soil orders in descending order of their share of India's area:
A. Alfisols
B. Entisols
C. Inceptisols
D. Vertisols
accepted.x: The shares are Inceptisols 39.7%, Entisols 28.1%, Alfisols 13.6% and Vertisols 8.5%, giving the order C, B, A, D.
accepted.tq: Arrange the categories by comparing their numerical shares from highest to lowest.
accepted.sec: ICAR/USDA classification - soil orders by area, soil profile horizons

accepted.s: Which one of the following soil orders is correctly matched with its approximate share of India's area?
accepted.x: Aridisols account for approximately 4.3% of India's area. Ultisols account for about 2.5%, Mollisols 0.4% and Vertisols 8.5%.
accepted.tq: Use the numerical table to detect the swapped percentage values.
accepted.sec: ICAR/USDA classification - soil orders by area, soil profile horizons

accepted.s: Which one of the following soil orders is the smallest in terms of its share of India's area?
accepted.x: Mollisols are the smallest listed soil order, occupying approximately 0.4% of India's area.
accepted.tq: Compare the lower end of the distribution rather than the largest categories.
accepted.sec: ICAR/USDA classification - soil orders by area, soil profile horizons

accepted.s:
In a soil profile, which sequence correctly matches the horizons with their principal characteristics?
1. O — organic litter
2. A — humus-rich topsoil
3. E — leached horizon
4. B — accumulation in subsoil
5. C — weathered parent material
6. R — bedrock
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All six pairings are correct: O is organic litter, A is humus-rich topsoil, E is leached, B is the accumulation or subsoil horizon, C is weathered parent material and R is bedrock.
accepted.tq: Verify each horizon-characteristic pair individually before selecting the complete option.
accepted.sec: ICAR/USDA classification - soil orders by area, soil profile horizons

accepted.s: The Soil Health Card scheme was launched on 19 February 2015 at:
accepted.x: The Soil Health Card scheme was launched on 19 February 2015 at Suratgarh in Rajasthan.
accepted.tq: Pair the launch date with the correct place rather than a prominent administrative centre.
accepted.sec: Soil Health Card scheme and soil testing

accepted.s: The slogan associated with the Soil Health Card scheme is:
accepted.x: The slogan of the Soil Health Card scheme is “Swasth Dharaa, Khet Haraa”.
accepted.tq: Test exact recall of the official slogan rather than its general theme.
accepted.sec: Soil Health Card scheme and soil testing

accepted.s: Since 2022–23, the Soil Health Card scheme has been included as which component of RKVY?
accepted.x: Since 2022–23, the scheme has been implemented as the Soil Health and Fertility component of the Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact administrative component instead of a related agricultural programme.
accepted.sec: Soil Health Card scheme and soil testing

accepted.s: How many parameters are tested under the Soil Health Card scheme?
accepted.x: Soil Health Cards test 12 parameters, including major nutrients, micronutrients and physical properties.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the exact count from nearby plausible programme figures.
accepted.sec: Soil Health Card scheme and soil testing

accepted.s: Which of the following groups contains only micronutrients tested under the Soil Health Card scheme?
o: Nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, sulphur and zinc
Calcium, magnesium, sodium, nitrogen and phosphorus
Carbon, oxygen, hydrogen, nitrogen and potassium
Zinc, iron, copper, manganese and boron
accepted.x: The micronutrients listed are zinc, iron, copper, manganese and boron. Nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium and sulphur are separately included among the tested nutrients.
accepted.tq: Separate the micronutrient list from the major nutrient list.
accepted.sec: Soil Health Card scheme and soil testing

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Soil Health Card generation and testing is correct?
o: 92.87 lakh cards were generated in 2025–26, while no sample collection was reported.
97.53 crore samples were collected in 2025–26 and all were tested.
25.79 lakh cards had been generated up to February 2026, with the highest number issued in Kerala.
25.79 crore cards had been generated up to February 2026, and Uttar Pradesh had issued the most cards.
accepted.x: Up to February 2026, 25.79 crore cards had been generated, and Uttar Pradesh had issued the largest number. In FY 2025–26, 97.53 lakh samples were collected and 92.87 lakh tested.
accepted.tq: Check the units, date and state ranking together to avoid number substitution.
accepted.sec: Soil Health Card scheme and soil testing

accepted.s: In FY 2025–26, the number of soil samples collected and tested under the Soil Health Card programme was respectively:
accepted.x: In FY 2025–26, 97.53 lakh samples were collected and 92.87 lakh samples were tested.
accepted.tq: Read the operational sequence carefully: collection precedes testing.
accepted.sec: Soil Health Card scheme and soil testing

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Village-Level Soil Testing Labs:
1. The target is 7,500 laboratories during 2023–26.
2. Assistance of ₹1.5 lakh is provided per laboratory.
3. ICAR is piloting rapid spectroscopic soil analysis.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The programme targets 7,500 Village-Level Soil Testing Labs during 2023–26, provides ₹1.5 lakh assistance per laboratory, and is complemented by ICAR's pilot of rapid spectroscopic soil analysis.
accepted.tq: Check the target, financial assistance and technological initiative as separate statements.
accepted.sec: Soil Health Card scheme and soil testing
